short: Controlling silk fibroin particle features for drug delivery
title: Controlling silk fibroin particle features for drug delivery

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Drug-delivery carriers need controllable size, secondary structure and surface charge to tune drug loading and release. Salting-out parameters (ionic strength, pH, protein concentration) should set silk particle features that govern loading and release.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/need), s2 (HYP/hypothesis), s3 (DES/base_system), s4 (DES/route), s5 (DES/variable_sweep), s6 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Mean particle size grows with silk concentration, ~0.5 um at 0.25 mg/mL to ~3.6 um at 20 mg/mL. Particle secondary structure shifts from silk II-rich (beta sheet) at pH 4-6 to silk I-rich at pH 8-9
states.detail: Absorbed: s8 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), s9 (STR/chemistry/bonding). Premises: Amide I ~1650 cm-1 marks silk I/random coil/helix; ~1620-1630 cm-1 marks silk II beta sheet

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: pH sets domain charges and chain extension, which set micelle packing and the secondary structure stabilised on particle formation. Particle zeta potential becomes more negative with production pH, about -26 mV (pH 4) to -46 mV (pH 9).
states.detail: Absorbed: s10 (MEC/pathway), s11 (PRP/value), s12 (PRP/value), s13 (MEC/pathway), s14 (PRP/value), s15 (PRP/value)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Silk particles act as tunable sustained-release carriers for positively charged small-molecule drugs

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Salting-out ionic strength, pH and silk concentration control particle size, secondary structure and charge, which set drug loading and release

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: Loading efficiency ~100% for crystal violet to ratio 60 and alcian blue to ratio 20, then falls (to 64% and 38%). Loading rises with molar ratio to ~13% (alcian blue), ~6.7% (crystal violet), ~4.5% (rhodamine B).
nodes.solves: Cationic drug loading is near-complete (~100% efficiency) up to ~6% matrix loading, then efficiency falls as the matrix saturates
nodes.op: compare across conditions, correlate across series, read trend
nodes.detail: o13: Loading efficiency ~100% for crystal violet to ratio 60 and alcian blue to ratio 20, then falls (to 64% and 38%); o14: Loading rises with molar ratio to ~13% (alcian blue), ~6.7% (crystal violet), ~4.5% (rhodamine B); a1: Rhodamine B loading efficiency only 68% falling to 48% at all molar ratios, never near 100%
nodes.inner_audit: a1: Rhodamine B loading efficiency only 68% falling to 48% at all molar ratios, never near 100%

nodes.title: ECHEM:CV, PHYS:particlesize, F6
nodes.head: Zeta potential rises with loading; alcian blue crosses zero between 6.6% and 8.1% loading, reaching +43 mV
nodes.solves: Cationic drugs load by charge-charge binding to negative silk; bound drug neutralises particle charge, ending uptake
nodes.note: linked text says zeta 'decreases' with loading; the plot shows the value increasing from -37 to +43 mV (magnitude of the negative charge decreases). CV and RhB (inset) rise from ~-45 to -20 / -14 mV
